correctness.rationale: Set s=r^h+1 and D=2(r-1). For a root y and any place above X=infinity, its negative valuation gives r times its pole order equal to es where e is the local ramification index. Since gcd(r,s)=1, r divides e; the extension degree is at most r, proving degree r, total ramification and unique infinity. The Y derivative -1 makes the affine model smooth, and monic reduction gives its k[X]-basis 1,Y,...,Y^(r-1). The congruences r^j=1 mod D on the supported indices and 2r=2 mod D give the stated faithful tame diagonal action. The full affine invariant ring is spanned by X^iY^j with i+2j=0 mod D, and pole orders upstairs ir+js are distinct by reduction modulo r. At the fixed infinity the index is D, so no leading-pole cancellation occurs downstairs either. For fixed j the least i gives a_j=r+jL for j>0, with a_0=0; other i add multiples of r downstairs. The relation DL=1 mod r makes these representatives exhaustive and distinct modulo r, giving the Apéry and Riemann–Roch assertions. Splitting a nonzero Apéry entry into two positive nongaps would either add a positive multiple of r to its own residue minimum, or use positive indices summing to j or j+r, already larger than a_j. Adding the generators to jL shows these and only these top residue gaps are pseudo-Frobenius. The genus sum is (r-1)(L+1)/2=(r^h-1)/4, and 2g=F+type gives almost symmetry; the type exceeds one. Independent finite enumeration of divisible upstairs pole orders corroborated the Apéry and gap formulas, including the nonprime case (r,h)=(9,2).
residual_risks: The arithmetic enumeration corroborates finite instances, not the geometric proof. Statements are geometric at the marked infinity only; no basis descent to an unspecified smaller field is asserted.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The construction paper and general gap papers do not establish coverage on their own. The twisted theorem dominates the prime-r slice on the very same cover for a wider range of f. The other indexed result is an index-two intermediate quotient of the target in the indicated regime, so is substantive related coverage rather than formally the same curve.

evidence: The twisted proof explicitly gives u and uv^j with the desired one-pole orders. The frozen monomials are u^k and u^k(uv^j). Distinct pole orders and the full Apéry set make this the one-point basis, although the twisted record does not state the complete basis in its Finding.

At r=p^e the same auxiliary cover is y^r-y=x f(x^(r-1)) with x^(r-1)=u, y=xv (in the frozen model, x=X^2, y=Y). Its right side has M=1+(r-1)d coprime to r. The degree-r total ramification and pole orders r,M follow by the same degree/valuation argument. The F_r^times scalar quotient uses the very same one-pole functions x^(r-1-j)y^j=uv^j with pole orders r+j(d-1). Completeness follows by the tame invariant-monomial decomposition, or the same genus comparison using the additive cover with one jump M.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prime basis, invariants, and almost-symmetry characterization are direct consequences of the recorded functions and Apéry set. The nonprime scope is outside the literal earlier statement, but the explicit reduction shows why simply restricting the frozen theorem to higher prime powers would not by itself introduce a nonroutine new scientific result.

evidence: The twisted RESULT.md Finding at offset 0 gives uv^p-v=f(u), d>=2, gcd(p,d-1)=1, unique infinity over u and the matching semigroup, minimal generators, Apéry set and type data. Its proof, offsets 2936–3777, identifies the quotient and the marked point.

For the frozen quotient set u=X^D and v=Y/X^2. Dividing the equation by X^2 gives u v^r-v=Σ_{j even} b_j u^((r^j-1)/D). This f has degree d=L+1, nonzero leading coefficient and constant b_0. Since adjoining X to k(u,v) recovers Y and gives degree at most D, faithfulness proves k(C)=k(u,v). The unique pole of u identifies the same marked point.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: For r=p the hypotheses of the twisted theorem are satisfied exactly and this is an isomorphism of pointed curves, not a coincidental equality of abstract numerical semigroups. Its Apéry formula transfers with d-1=L. Its prime-exponent theorem does not literally cover e>1.

originality.rationale: There is verified equivalent coverage of the entire prime-r case, including the primary application singled out in the Finding. The same-day twisted Artin–Schreier record 60088f5a2835 treats this very marked curve in invariant coordinates and is broader in f for r=p. Its pole functions also furnish the stated basis by taking powers of u and using its Apéry theorem. Same-day ordering is unresolved, so this is not a priority allegation. The other stated scope, r=p^e for e>1, is not literally asserted in that record. But no material distinct theorem is established by that extension here: the same twisted-cover construction and pole calculation extend directly using the additive group of F_r and scalar group F_r^times, with gcd(r,d-1)=1. This is a scope extension, not evidence that the prime-power theorem was explicitly published there.
residual_risks: The order of the same-day records is not established, and no priority allegation is made. The higher-prime-power theorem is not literally in the matched record; the assessment of its extension as routine follows from the explicit reduction, not from a search miss. The Sepúlveda–Tizziotti full text was unavailable.

value.rationale: One-point Riemann–Roch bases on these curves are useful, and the proof is correct. But the advertised prime-field maximal family is already covered by the exact twisted-curve theorem, including the basis as a direct consequence of its pole functions. The remaining prime-power scope uses the same scalar quotient and degree/coprimality pole argument without a new mathematical obstruction or independent application substantiated by the record. The marginal contribution is a routine extension and restatement of a covered narrow invariant; no separate valuable repair was established.
residual_risks: This is a judgment of the frozen contribution beyond established coverage, not a denial that the formulas are useful, nor a claim that all nonprime cases were already explicit in the comparison record.
